content.title: Oklahoma City Thunder vs Boston Celtics injury report: Who's playing, injured and questionable players, head-to-head records, team stats, and more (March 25, 2026)
content.text: Boston Celtics' Jayson Tatum vs Oklahoma City Thunder's Shai (Image via Getty)The Oklahoma City Thunder play the Boston Celtics at TD Garden on March 25, 2026. It brings together one of the top teams in the Western Conference and a strong side from the East. Oklahoma City comes in with one of the best records in the league, while Boston continues to rely on its home record to stay in position in the standings.This game matters for both teams as the regular season moves toward its final stretch. Playoff seeding is still in play, and both sides need wins to secure their spots. Oklahoma City has had better results in recent meetings, but Boston’s experience and depth keep this matchup balanced.Oklahoma City Thunder and Boston Celtics Injury report (March 25, 2026)Both teams enter the game with very few injury concerns, so most of the main players are expected to be available.Oklahoma City Thunder (57-15): • Thomas Sorber: Out for the season (right knee ACL tear)The rest of the Thunder squad is available, including Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Chet Holmgren, and Cason Wallace.Israel Iran WarUS-Israel-Iran War News Live Updates: Amazon Web Services 'disrupted' following drone attack in Bahrain; Saudi, UAE mull joining Iran war82nd Airborne Division to be deployed in Middle East: Inside America’s fastest strike force that once stormed Nazi-occupied France'Lack of permission': Iran turns back Pakistan-bound ship trying to pass through Strait of HormuzBoston Celtics (47-24): • Nikola Vucevic: Out (right ring finger fracture, expected return mid-April)Boston has the rest of its roster available, with Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown set to play.Oklahoma City Thunder and Boston Celtics Projected rotations and depth breakdown (March 25, 2026)Oklahoma City continues to depend on a young group that focuses on scoring and defense. The starting lineup includes Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Cason Wallace, Luguentz Dort, Chet Holmgren, and Isaiah Hartenstein. The bench includes Isaiah Joe, Aaron Wiggins, Ajay Mitchell, Alex Caruso, and Jaylin Williams, providing support across positions.Boston relies on an experienced lineup built around spacing and versatility. Jrue Holiday, Derrick White, Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum, and Kristaps Porzingis form the starting five. The bench includes Payton Pritchard, Neemias Queta, Sam Hauser, Baylor Scheierman, and Al Horford.Oklahoma City Thunder and Boston Celtics Head-to-head record and recent trendBoston leads the all-time series with a 79-69 record over 148 regular-season games. However, Oklahoma City has won the last three meetings between the teams, including a 104-102 result on March 12 this season.Oklahoma City Thunder and Boston Celtics Team performance comparisonCategoryOklahoma City ThunderBoston Celtics Record 57-15 47-24 PPG 118.7 (5th) 114.1 (22nd) Opp PPG 107.5 (2nd) 107.0 (1st) RPG 44.1 (13th) 46.5 (4th) 3PM/G 13.6 (14th, 36.1%) 15.2 (3rd, 36%) Net Rating +11.2 +7.1Oklahoma City ranks high in scoring and defense, while Boston stands out in rebounding and three-point shooting volume.Oklahoma City Thunder and Boston Celtics Recent form and key contributorsIn the last 20 games, Oklahoma City has seen steady production from multiple players. Chet Holmgren has averaged 13.7 points, 8.6 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has averaged 16.6 points and 4.1 assists. Isaiah Joe has added 13.6 points with 2.9 three-pointers per game.Boston’s output has come mainly from its top players. Jaylen Brown has averaged 23.5 points and 5.5 assists. Derrick White has contributed 16.5 points, 2.6 three-pointers, and 1.4 blocks. Payton Pritchard has averaged 14.6 points and 4.9 assists.Oklahoma City Thunder and Boston Celtics Season leaders and matchup outlookShai Gilgeous-Alexander leads Oklahoma City with 31.5 points per game, second in the league. Chet Holmgren averages 9 rebounds per game. For Boston, Jaylen Brown scores between 28.5 and 29.6 points per game. Neemias Queta averages just over eight rebounds, while Derrick White records 5.3 assists and 1.3 steals.Both teams are close to full strength. Oklahoma City’s pace and scoring will be tested by Boston’s structure and defense. The game is expected to be competitive and important for both sides.
